[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IDBRKR-2.7.26.md#abb-context]

### ABB Context

- **Parent L2 Capability**: Application Authentication & Authorization — [GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02](../GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02.md)
- **ABB Catalog**: [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06](../GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06.md)
- **Capability Statement**: The enterprise SHALL have an architectural capability to mediate authentication between application components and identity providers, abstracting the identity protocol details from application logic and enabling consistent identity federation across application boundaries.
page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IDBRKR-2.7.26.md#abb-scope]

### ABB Scope

**In Scope**:
- Architectural capability to federate authentication between applications and one or more identity sources
- Protocol translation between application authentication needs and identity provider capabilities
- Session establishment and management at the application layer for authenticated principals
- Single sign-on pattern enablement across related application components

**Out of Scope**:
- Enterprise workforce identity lifecycle management, directory services, and MFA enrollment (see Identity Security domain)
- Authorization policy evaluation (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-TOKVAL-2.7.27 and GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIAZ-2.7.12)
- Machine-to-machine credential management (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-VAULT-2.7.21 and GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DSECR-2.7.22)
- Security controls, configuration baselines (`standards/security/`)

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IDBRKR-2.7.26.md#core-principles]

### Core Principles

- Application authentication SHALL NOT require applications to implement identity protocol logic directly — authentication SHALL be delegated to a broker capability.
- The broker SHALL support open, widely-adopted identity federation protocols to enable interoperability with enterprise and external identity providers.
- Applications SHOULD receive identity assertions in a standardized token format, irrespective of the upstream identity protocol used.
- Session management at the application layer SHALL enforce session expiry and provide a mechanism for session termination.
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IDBRKR-2.7.26.md#identity-federation]

#### Identity Federation

**Architectural intent**: Enable applications to accept authenticated identities from the enterprise identity provider and external identity sources without implementing protocol logic themselves.

**Design guidance**:
- The broker SHALL support federation with the enterprise identity provider as the primary identity source.
- Protocol translation SHALL be transparent to consuming applications; applications SHALL receive a consistent assertion format regardless of upstream identity source.
- Federation configuration SHALL be managed through a governed change process.
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IDBRKR-2.7.26.md#application-session-management]

#### Application Session Management

**Architectural intent**: Manage authenticated sessions at the application layer with appropriate lifetime controls.

**Design guidance**:
- Application sessions SHALL have a defined maximum lifetime.
- Idle session timeout SHALL be configurable and applied consistently.
- A session termination mechanism (logout) SHALL be provided and SHALL invalidate the session token.
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IDBRKR-2.7.26.md#consistent-token-issuance]

#### Consistent Token Issuance

**Architectural intent**: Provide application components with standardized identity assertions that can be validated without per-application protocol implementation.

**Design guidance**:
- Identity tokens issued to applications SHALL follow a consistent format and claims structure.
- Token validation SHOULD be handled by GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-TOKVAL-2.7.27 rather than by individual application components.
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IDBRKR-2.7.26.md#integration-interfaces]

### Integration Interfaces

| Interface | Direction | Consuming ABB | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Authentication Request | Inbound | End User / Application Component | Authentication initiation from application |
| Enterprise IdP | Outbound | Enterprise Identity Provider | Federation protocol exchange with identity source |
| Identity Token | Outbound | Application / GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-TOKVAL-2.7.27 | Standardized identity assertion issued to consumer |
| Session Cookie / Token | Bidirectional | Browser / Application Client | Session establishment and validation |
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IDBRKR-2.7.26.md#zero-trust-alignment-nist-sp-800-207]

### Zero Trust Alignment (NIST SP 800-207)

The Application Identity Broker is a direct implementation of the Identity pillar of Zero Trust at the application layer — ensuring that every principal interacting with an application is authenticated through a verified, governed identity source rather than relying on network-based trust assumptions.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IDBRKR-2.7.26.md#nist-sp-800-53-intent-alignment]

### NIST SP 800-53 Intent Alignment

This ABB enables the architectural intent of the IA (Identification and Authentication) family — specifically user and service identification and authentication — and the AC (Access Control) family's session management requirements.
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IDBRKR-2.7.26.md#constraints-and-dependencies]

### Constraints and Dependencies

- The broker depends on the enterprise identity provider being available and accessible; architecture must address availability requirements.
- Session management at the application layer must be consistent with enterprise session policy; architectural coordination with the Identity Security domain is required.
- This ABB works in conjunction with GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-TOKVAL-2.7.27 — the broker establishes identity; token validation enforces claims on each subsequent request.
